This `useEffect` performs side effects (it calls `clearMoneyRequest(...)` to delete draft transactions and `Navigation.navigate(...)`) while suppressing `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`. Suppressing the dependency lint hides the effect's real dependencies — `draftTransactionIDs` and `detailsPageRouteObject` — so if either changes without `lockedExpenseChatReportID` changing, the effect will not re-run and may act on stale data (clearing the wrong drafts or navigating with an outdated route object).

Either include all captured values in the dependency array so the effect stays in sync, or restructure so the mutation/navigation is triggered from an event/guarded flow rather than an effect with a suppressed dependency check. If the omission is truly intentional, document why the omitted deps cannot change during this flow so the race-condition risk is explicitly ruled out.

Same issue as the native counterpart: `showConfirmModal` returns a Promise whose `.then()` performs navigation side effects inside a `useEffect` with no cleanup mechanism. If the effect's dependencies change while the modal is showing, the stale `.then()` callback will still execute, potentially navigating at an unexpected time.

Add an `ignore` flag with a cleanup function to guard the `.then()` callback against stale executions, as described in the native file comment.

`conciergeReportID` is captured in the closure of this mount-only useEffect (dependency array is `[]` with `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` suppressed). Since this effect runs once on mount and `useOnyx(ONYXKEYS.CONCIERGE_REPORT_ID)` loads asynchronously, `conciergeReportID` will almost certainly be `undefined` when this closure is created. The value will never be refreshed because the effect never re-runs. This is PERF-15 Case 2: the eslint-disable hides a dependency that could change.

The same fix as above applies: read `conciergeReportID` from Onyx at the point of use (e.g., via `Onyx.connect` in the notification module) instead of capturing it in a one-time closure. This ensures the current value is always used when a notification is triggered, regardless of when Onyx finishes loading.
